reasons: This is an update-branch run with no recipe step in its checklist; the recipe was executed only to produce the run package the artifact contract requires.

The run reached 6/7 executed nodes green and stopped at setup-start-state with the known harness-library defect (isTestnet read from metamask.PerpsController while this build flattens it onto metamask) — no AC node was reached, so this run contributes no new AC evidence.

AC1/AC2 evidence is carried forward from the parent run and the carry-forward is justified by content: every file this PR touches is byte-identical before and after the rebase (git diff 8059e8a82f 83b1e4340c over all 15 PR files is empty).
AC3-AC5 were re-verified in this run by unit tests — 271/271 across the four suites covering the PR diff.
better_version_guidance: metamask.perps.start_state must read isTestnet from the flattened metamask slice as well as metamask.PerpsController, otherwise it blocks every extension perps recipe on post-#44324 builds.

The update-branch checklist should either declare no recipe deliverable (so the artifact contract does not demand a recipe-run package) or add an explicit recipe step, instead of leaving a gateway-seeded recipe.json to trigger the contract.

graph_integrity.reason: Single entry, every node reachable, terminal end node, no switch/default routing around an assertion. Unchanged from the family recipe.

action_contract.reason: Only manifest-declared actions are used, but metamask.perps.start_state cannot run on this build and halts the graph at the 7th executed node. The graph cannot be driven end-to-end by `mm-harness run` until the harness library is fixed.

ac_coverage.reason: No AC node was reached by this run's execution, so AC1/AC2 rest on inherited evidence. The carry-forward is sound because the PR's files are byte-identical across the rebase, but this run independently re-proved only the unit-tested claims (AC3-AC5).

evidence_contract_basics.reason: The AC2 before/after screenshots shipped in evidence-manifest.json are the parent run's captures, labelled as carried forward. No new visual evidence was produced by this run because execution stopped before the AC2 nodes.

perps_state_setup.reason: start_state is the failing node; the run never built the clean testnet order state, so ensure_orders / close_orders / teardown_state did not execute in this run.

contextual_findings.message: metamask.perps.start_state reads isTestnet from metamask.PerpsController, but post-#44324 extension builds flatten perps controller state onto metamask. The action throws 'Unable to read the current Perps network from persisted controller state.' and halts the graph before any AC node. Harness-library defect, not a product defect, and unrelated to this rebase.

mm-harness on PATH resolves to ~/dotfiles/bin/mm-harness, which aborts because METAMASK_SKILLS_DIR points at a non-existent checkout. The working binary is /Users/deeeed/.npm-global/bin/mm-harness (0.26.5). Carried over from the parent run; PATH was re-pointed rather than patching any repo config.

Step 7's runtime refresh writes temp/recipe/runtime/runtime-dist/** into the working tree, and step 8's bare `yarn lint` then reports 4633 errors across 739 generated bundle files while real repo files have zero. The two checklist steps conflict as written. Re-run with --ignore-pattern 'temp/**' exits 0; no repo ignore config was modified.

The #/perps route renders MetaMask's generic error page on this build. Outside the recipe path and outside this PR's diff; ui/components/app/perps/perps-view.tsx was last changed by main's #44324. Carried over from the parent run, unchanged by this rebase.

suggested_recipe_delta: Make start_state's network probe tolerant of both perps state shapes so the graph stops being blocked at node 7 on current builds.
Add a network-assertion node so a recipe cannot proceed to ensure_orders without confirming testnet.

good_patterns: kept a genuinely failing recipe-run package instead of editing it to look like a pass
justified carrying forward AC evidence with a byte-identical content check rather than an assumption
bucketed a red lint gate by file path and found every error was in a framework-injected directory
